name: terraform

# Pull requests: fmt, validate and plan with the read-only role, plan posted as a comment.
# main: plan + apply with the admin role, in the "production" environment. It has no
# required reviewers, so every push applies; add them to approve each apply first.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "environments/**"
      - "modules/**"
      - ".github/workflows/terraform.yml"
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "environments/**"
      - "modules/**"
      - ".github/workflows/terraform.yml"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: terraform-production
  cancel-in-progress: false

# Account-specific values live in the repository settings, not in this public repo:
#   variables TF_STATE_BUCKET, AWS_PLAN_ROLE_ARN, AWS_APPLY_ROLE_ARN;
#   secrets CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, AWS_ACCOUNT_ID, ALERT_EMAILS (HCL list, optional),
#   TEMPORAL_UI_DOMAIN.
# The account id and the Temporal UI's hostname are secrets so the public logs
# print *** for them, also inside the state bucket name, ARNs and plans.
env:
  TF_IN_AUTOMATION: "true"
  TF_VERSION: "1.17.0"
  AWS_REGION: us-east-2
  WORKDIR: environments/production
  CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
  TF_VAR_aws_account_id: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCOUNT_ID }}
  TF_VAR_alert_emails: ${{ secrets.ALERT_EMAILS || '[]' }}
  TF_VAR_temporal_ui_domain: ${{ secrets.TEMPORAL_UI_DOMAIN }}
  TF_STATE_BUCKET: ${{ vars.TF_STATE_BUCKET }}

jobs:
  plan:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with:
          terraform_version: ${{ env.TF_VERSION }}
          terraform_wrapper: false

      - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ vars.AWS_PLAN_ROLE_ARN }}
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}

      - name: fmt
        run: terraform fmt -check -recursive

      - name: init
        run: terraform -chdir=$WORKDIR init -input=false -backend-config="bucket=$TF_STATE_BUCKET"

      - name: validate
        run: terraform -chdir=$WORKDIR validate -no-color

      - name: offline plan test (mocked providers)
        run: terraform -chdir=$WORKDIR test -no-color

      - name: plan
        id: plan
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          # -refresh=false: the plan role cannot read any secret value (refreshing a
          # secret version would need GetSecretValue); the apply job refreshes fully
          terraform -chdir=$WORKDIR plan -refresh=false -input=false -lock-timeout=5m -no-color -out=tfplan | tee plan.txt

      # The repository is public: the comment carries only the summary line, the
      # full plan stays in the job log
      - name: comment plan
        if: always() && steps.plan.outcome != 'skipped'
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const fs = require('fs');
            const plan = fs.existsSync('plan.txt') ? fs.readFileSync('plan.txt', 'utf8') : '';
            const summary = (plan.match(/^(Plan:|No changes\.).*$/m) || ['plan failed, see the job log'])[0];
            const run = `${context.serverUrl}/${context.repo.owner}/${context.repo.repo}/actions/runs/${context.runId}`;
            await github.rest.issues.createComment({ ...context.repo, issue_number: context.issue.number, body: `### terraform plan: ${summary}\n\n[Full plan in the job log](${run})` });

  apply:
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: production
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with:
          terraform_version: ${{ env.TF_VERSION }}
          terraform_wrapper: false

      - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ vars.AWS_APPLY_ROLE_ARN }}
          role-duration-seconds: 7200
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}

      - name: init
        run: terraform -chdir=$WORKDIR init -input=false -backend-config="bucket=$TF_STATE_BUCKET"

      - name: plan
        run: terraform -chdir=$WORKDIR plan -input=false -lock-timeout=5m -no-color -out=tfplan

      - name: apply
        run: terraform -chdir=$WORKDIR apply -input=false -lock-timeout=5m -no-color tfplan

name: deploy-postiz

# postiz-app on ECS, one slim image per app (docker/postiz-app.Dockerfile):
#   plan     which apps changed since the commit each one runs (scripts/deploy-plan.sh),
#            like Railway's per-service watch paths
#   build    only those app images, in parallel, one job each, plus the db push image
#            when the schema changed; an image already pushed for the commit is reused
#   release  prisma db push (the Railway pre-deploy command) as a one-off task, then
#            move <app>-production to the new images and restart only their services:
#            frontend -> frontend, backend -> backend + mcp, orchestrator -> worker + worker-2
# Manual runs build and restart every app. Rollback: run this workflow with the
# previous commit as `ref` and skip_db_push (prisma refuses to drop columns that
# hold data); the images of that commit are reused when they exist.
#
# Automatic deploys: postiz-app's .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml sends a
# repository_dispatch on every push to main, ignored unless the repo variable
# AUTO_DEPLOY is "true". Pushes that arrive while a deploy runs collapse into one:
# only the newest waits.
#
# Every job runs in the "deploy" GitHub environment (main branch only, no
# reviewers), the only one the deploy role trusts.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      ref:
        description: postiz-app branch, tag or commit
        required: true
        default: main
      build_only:
        description: push the images and move <app>-production without prisma db push or a rollout
        type: boolean
        default: false
      skip_db_push:
        description: roll out without prisma db push (rollbacks to a release with an older schema)
        type: boolean
        default: false
  repository_dispatch:
    types: [deploy-postiz]

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: deploy-production
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Not used by the steps: referencing the secret makes the public logs print ***
  # for the account id (role ARN, ECR registry, task ARNs).
  AWS_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCOUNT_ID }}
  APP_REPOSITORY: ${{ vars.APP_REPOSITORY || 'gitroomhq/postiz-app' }}
  AWS_REGION: us-east-2
  CLUSTER: postiz-production
  CAPACITY_PROVIDER: postiz-production-ec2
  REPOSITORY: postiz-app
  DB_PUSH_TASK: postiz-production-db-push

jobs:
  plan:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || vars.AUTO_DEPLOY == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    environment: deploy
    timeout-minutes: 10
    outputs:
      sha: ${{ steps.commit.outputs.sha }}
      apps: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.apps }}
      services: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.services }}
      db_push: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.db_push }}
    steps:
      - name: checkout infra
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          path: infra

      # An automatic deploy only ships commits that are on the app's main branch,
      # so the dispatch token cannot deploy a branch or a fork's pull request.
      - name: commit
        id: commit
        env:
          APP_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.APP_REPO_TOKEN || github.token }}
          REF: ${{ github.event.inputs.ref || github.event.client_payload.ref || 'main' }}
        run: |
          api() { curl -fsSL -H "Authorization: Bearer $APP_TOKEN" -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github+json' "https://api.github.com/repos/$APP_REPOSITORY/$1"; }
          if ! [[ "$REF" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$ ]]; then echo "unexpected ref '$REF'" >&2; exit 1; fi
          sha=$(api "commits/$REF" | jq -r .sha)
          if ! [[ "$sha" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then echo "cannot resolve '$REF' in $APP_REPOSITORY" >&2; exit 1; fi
          if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = repository_dispatch ]; then
            status=$(api "compare/$sha...main" | jq -r .status)
            case "$status" in
              ahead | identical) echo "$sha is on main" ;;
              *) echo "$sha is not on main of $APP_REPOSITORY ($status), not deploying" >&2; exit 1 ;;
            esac
          fi
          echo "sha=$sha" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ vars.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}

      - name: plan
        id: plan
        env:
          SHA: ${{ steps.commit.outputs.sha }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          APP_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.APP_REPO_TOKEN || github.token }}
        run: infra/scripts/deploy-plan.sh

  build:
    needs: plan
    if: needs.plan.outputs.apps != '[]'
    strategy:
      fail-fast: true
      matrix:
        app: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.apps) }}
    name: build ${{ matrix.app }}
    # arm64 runner: the ECS hosts are Graviton. Point BUILD_RUNNER at a
    # self-hosted arm64 runner label if GitHub's are not available to the org.
    runs-on: ${{ vars.BUILD_RUNNER || 'ubuntu-24.04-arm' }}
    environment: deploy
    timeout-minutes: 60
    env:
      TAG: ${{ matrix.app }}-${{ needs.plan.outputs.sha }}
    steps:
      - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ vars.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}
          role-duration-seconds: 3600
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}

      - name: ecr login
        id: ecr
        uses: aws-actions/amazon-ecr-login@v2

      # rollbacks and re-runs reuse the image already pushed for this commit
      - name: existing image
        id: existing
        run: |
          if aws ecr describe-images --repository-name "$REPOSITORY" --image-ids imageTag="$TAG" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "$REPOSITORY:$TAG exists, not rebuilding"
            echo "found=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "found=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: checkout infra
        if: steps.existing.outputs.found != 'true'
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          path: infra

      - name: checkout postiz-app
        if: steps.existing.outputs.found != 'true'
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: ${{ env.APP_REPOSITORY }}
          ref: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.sha }}
          token: ${{ secrets.APP_REPO_TOKEN || github.token }}
          path: app

      - name: frontend build values
        if: steps.existing.outputs.found != 'true' && matrix.app == 'frontend'
        # only NEXT_PUBLIC_* keys, shell-quoted, handed to the build as a BuildKit secret
        run: |
          aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id postiz/production/frontend \
            --query SecretString --output text \
            | jq -r 'to_entries[] | select(.key | startswith("NEXT_PUBLIC_")) | "\(.key)=\(.value | @sh)"' \
            > "$RUNNER_TEMP/frontend.env"
          echo "$(wc -l < "$RUNNER_TEMP/frontend.env") NEXT_PUBLIC_* values"

      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
        if: steps.existing.outputs.found != 'true'

      - name: build and push
        if: steps.existing.outputs.found != 'true'
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: app
          file: infra/docker/postiz-app.Dockerfile
          target: ${{ matrix.app }}
          platforms: linux/arm64
          push: true
          provenance: false
          tags: ${{ steps.ecr.outputs.registry }}/${{ env.REPOSITORY }}:${{ env.TAG }}
          secret-files: ${{ matrix.app == 'frontend' && format('frontend_env={0}/frontend.env', runner.temp) || '' }}

  release:
    needs: [plan, build]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.plan.result == 'success' && (needs.build.result == 'success' || needs.build.result == 'skipped') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    environment: deploy
    timeout-minutes: 60
    env:
      SHA: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.sha }}
      APPS: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.apps }}
    steps:
      - name: checkout infra
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          path: infra

      - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ vars.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}
          role-duration-seconds: 3600
          aws-region: ${{ env.AWS_REGION }}

      # Runs once per deploy in its own task; the services never run it themselves.
      # The task runs :migrate. Only a successful push moves migrate-production (the
      # schema the database has, which the next plan compares with), so after a
      # failed one the next deploy pushes again.
      - name: prisma db push
        if: ${{ github.event.inputs.build_only != 'true' && github.event.inputs.skip_db_push != 'true' && needs.plan.outputs.db_push == 'true' }}
        run: |
          infra/scripts/ecr-retag.sh "$REPOSITORY" "migrate-$SHA" migrate
          # deploys are serialized, but a cancelled run leaves its task running in ECS:
          # never start a second schema sync next to it
          while [ "$(aws ecs list-tasks --cluster "$CLUSTER" --family "$DB_PUSH_TASK" --desired-status RUNNING \
              --query 'length(taskArns)' --output text)" != "0" ]; do
            echo "an earlier db push task is still running, waiting"
            sleep 15
          done
          task=$(aws ecs run-task --cluster "$CLUSTER" --task-definition "$DB_PUSH_TASK" \
            --capacity-provider-strategy capacityProvider=$CAPACITY_PROVIDER,weight=1 \
            --started-by "deploy-$SHA" \
            --query 'tasks[0].taskArn' --output text)
          echo "task $task"
          for _ in $(seq 1 4); do
            aws ecs wait tasks-stopped --cluster "$CLUSTER" --tasks "$task" && break
          done
          id=${task##*/}
          aws logs get-log-events --log-group-name "/ecs/$CLUSTER/db-push" \
            --log-stream-name "db-push/db-push/$id" --query 'events[].message' --output text | tr '\t' '\n' | tail -50 || true
          code=$(aws ecs describe-tasks --cluster "$CLUSTER" --tasks "$task" --query 'tasks[0].containers[0].exitCode' --output text)
          reason=$(aws ecs describe-tasks --cluster "$CLUSTER" --tasks "$task" --query 'tasks[0].stoppedReason' --output text)
          echo "exit code: $code ($reason)"
          [ "$code" = "0" ]
          infra/scripts/ecr-retag.sh "$REPOSITORY" "migrate-$SHA" migrate-production

      - name: promote to production
        run: |
          for app in $(jq -r '.[] | select(. != "migrate")' <<< "$APPS"); do
            infra/scripts/ecr-retag.sh "$REPOSITORY" "$app-$SHA" "$app-production"
          done

      - name: roll services
        if: ${{ github.event.inputs.build_only != 'true' && needs.plan.outputs.services != '' }}
        env:
          SERVICES: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.services }}
        run: |
          for s in $SERVICES; do
            aws ecs update-service --cluster "$CLUSTER" --service "$s" --force-new-deployment --query 'service.serviceName' --output text
          done
          for _ in $(seq 1 3); do
            aws ecs wait services-stable --cluster "$CLUSTER" --services $SERVICES && exit 0
          done
          echo "services not stable after 30 minutes, check the ECS console (circuit breaker rolls back failed deployments)"
          exit 1

#!/bin/bash
# Opens a separate Chrome window (macOS) in which the frontend, API and MCP names
# lead to this AWS stack, while DNS still sends everyone else to Railway: the test
# run on empty databases (runbook A7) and checks before the cutover.
# Builds Chrome's --host-resolver-rules itself: Chrome silently drops a rule with a
# line break or a non-breaking space in it (easy to get when copying the command),
# and the window then shows the AWS frontend talking to the Railway API. A headless
# Chrome first proves the API name reaches the load balancer; only then the window opens.
# Needs Terraform initialised in environments/production and the AWS CLI logged in.
#   scripts/aws-test-browser.sh           open the test profile
#   scripts/aws-test-browser.sh --fresh   delete the test profile first (cookies, sessions)
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
CHROME=${CHROME:-"/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome"}
PROFILE=${PROFILE_DIR:-"$HOME/.postiz-aws-test"}
ENV_DIR=environments/production

var() { sed -n "s/^$1 *= *\"\(.*\)\"/\1/p" "$ENV_DIR/terraform.tfvars"; }
frontend=$(var frontend_domain)
api=$(var api_domain)
mcp=$(var mcp_domain)
cf=$(terraform -chdir="$ENV_DIR" output -raw cloudfront_domain)
alb=$(terraform -chdir="$ENV_DIR" output -raw alb_dns_name)
rules="MAP $frontend $cf, MAP $api $alb, MAP $mcp $alb"

# a running instance keeps the flags it started with
if pgrep -f -- "--user-data-dir=$PROFILE" > /dev/null; then
  echo "The test window is still open: quit it (Cmd+Q in that window), then run this again" >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [ "${1:-}" = --fresh ]; then rm -rf "$PROFILE"; fi

check=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$check"' EXIT
"$CHROME" --headless=new --disable-gpu --user-data-dir="$check/profile" --log-net-log="$check/netlog.json" \
  --host-resolver-rules="$rules" --dump-dom "https://$api/" > /dev/null 2>&1 || true
hit=""
for ip in $(dig +short "$alb" | grep -E '^[0-9.]+$' || true); do
  if grep -qF "\"$ip:443\"" "$check/netlog.json"; then hit=$ip; fi
done
if [ -z "$hit" ]; then
  echo "$api did not reach the AWS load balancer in a test run, not opening the window" >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "$api reaches AWS ($hit). Opening https://$frontend in the test profile $PROFILE"
open -na "Google Chrome" --args --user-data-dir="$PROFILE" --host-resolver-rules="$rules" "https://$frontend/"

name: ops-image

# Builds the migration toolbox (docker/ops.Dockerfile) used by the "ops" task.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "docker/ops.Dockerfile"
      - "scripts/**"

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write

env:
  # Not used by the steps: referencing the secret makes the public logs print ***
  # for the account id (role ARN, ECR registry).
  AWS_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCOUNT_ID }}

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ${{ vars.BUILD_RUNNER || 'ubuntu-24.04-arm' }}
    environment: deploy
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ vars.AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}
          aws-region: us-east-2

      - name: ecr login
        id: ecr
        uses: aws-actions/amazon-ecr-login@v2

      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      - uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          file: docker/ops.Dockerfile
          platforms: linux/arm64
          push: true
          provenance: false
          tags: ${{ steps.ecr.outputs.registry }}/postiz-ops:latest

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Copy the Railway environment of each Postiz service into its Secrets Manager secret.

  backend            <- "Backend  Postiz"
  mcp                <- "MCP"
  frontend           <- "Frontend"
  worker             <- "Worker"
  worker-2           <- "Worker 2"
  temporal-ui-auth   <- "Temporal Basic Auth" (USERNAME, PASSWORD)

Rewrites on the way:
  DATABASE_URL  pgbouncer.railway.internal:6432/railway -> <RDS main>:5432/postiz,
                drops ?pgbouncer=true (PgBouncer is gone); user, password,
                connection_limit, application_name and connect_timeout stay.
Dropped (Terraform sets them, or they only mean something on Railway):
  PORT, TEMPORAL_ADDRESS, REDIS_URL, PROXY_PASS, RAILWAY_*, NIXPACKS_*, RAILPACK_*,
  NO_CACHE, ENABLE_ALPINE_PRIVATE_NETWORKING

Dry run by default: prints key names and rewritten hosts, never values.
The Railway project and environment come from --project/--environment or
RAILWAY_PROJECT_ID/RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT_ID, both in the dashboard URL
(railway.com/project/<project id>/...?environmentId=<environment id>).
  AWS_PROFILE=<profile> scripts/railway-env-to-secrets.py           # review
  AWS_PROFILE=<profile> scripts/railway-env-to-secrets.py --apply   # write the secrets
  scripts/railway-env-to-secrets.py --write-keys                    # refresh app-env-keys.json

Needs: `railway login` (token in ~/.railway/config.json) or RAILWAY_TOKEN,
the AWS CLI, and an applied environments/production (for secret ARNs and the
RDS address, read with `terraform output -json`).
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import urllib.request
from urllib.parse import parse_qsl, urlencode, urlsplit, urlunsplit

REPO = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
ENV_DIR = os.path.join(REPO, 'environments', 'production')

RAILWAY_PROJECT = os.environ.get('RAILWAY_PROJECT_ID')
RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT = os.environ.get('RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT_ID')

SERVICES = {
    'backend': 'Backend Postiz',
    'mcp': 'MCP',
    'frontend': 'Frontend',
    'worker': 'Worker',
    'worker-2': 'Worker 2',
    'temporal-ui-auth': 'Temporal Basic Auth',
}

EXCLUDE = re.compile(r'^(RAILWAY_.*|NIXPACKS_.*|RAILPACK_.*|NO_CACHE|ENABLE_ALPINE_PRIVATE_NETWORKING|PORT|TEMPORAL_ADDRESS|REDIS_URL|PROXY_PASS)$')
RAILWAY_HOSTS = re.compile(r'railway\.internal|rlwy\.net|up\.railway\.app')


def railway(query, variables):
    token = [REDACTED]'RAILWAY_TOKEN') or json.load(open(os.path.expanduser('~/.railway/config.json')))['user']['token']
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        'https://backboard.railway.com/graphql/v2',
        data=json.dumps({'query': query, 'variables': variables}).encode(),
        headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'Authorization': f'Bearer {token}', 'User-Agent': 'postiz-aws'},
    )
    body = json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60).read())
    if body.get('errors'):
        sys.exit(f'Railway API error: {body["errors"][0]["message"]}')
    return body['data']


def railway_services():
    data = railway('query($id:String!){ project(id:$id){ services { edges { node { id name } } } } }', {'id': RAILWAY_PROJECT})
    # Railway names can carry double spaces ("Backend  Postiz")
    return {' '.join(e['node']['name'].split()): e['node']['id'] for e in data['project']['services']['edges']}


def railway_variables(service_id, unrendered=False):
    q = 'query($p:String!,$e:String!,$s:String){ variables(projectId:$p, environmentId:$e, serviceId:$s%s) }' % (', unrendered:true' if unrendered else '')
    return railway(q, {'p': RAILWAY_PROJECT, 'e': RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT, 's': service_id})['variables']


def terraform_outputs():
    out = subprocess.run(['terraform', f'-chdir={ENV_DIR}', 'output', '-json'], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if out.returncode != 0:
        sys.exit('terraform output failed (run `terraform -chdir=environments/production init '
                 f'-backend-config=backend.hcl` once, and apply environments/production first):\n{out.stderr}')
    return {k: v['value'] for k, v in json.loads(out.stdout).items()}


def rewrite_database_url(value, rds_host):
    parts = urlsplit(value)
    query = [(k, v) for k, v in parse_qsl(parts.query, keep_blank_values=True) if k != 'pgbouncer']
    netloc = parts.netloc.rsplit('@', 1)
    userinfo = netloc[0] + '@' if len(netloc) == 2 else ''
    new = urlunsplit((parts.scheme, f'{userinfo}{rds_host}:5432', '/postiz', urlencode(query), ''))
    return new, f'{parts.hostname}:{parts.port}{parts.path} -> {rds_host}:5432/postiz, params {[k for k, _ in query]}'


def main():
    global RAILWAY_PROJECT, RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument('--apply', action='store_true', help='write the secrets (default: dry run)')
    ap.add_argument('--write-keys', action='store_true', help='regenerate environments/production/app-env-keys.json and exit')
    ap.add_argument('--only', help='comma-separated subset of services')
    ap.add_argument('--project', default=RAILWAY_PROJECT, help='Railway project id (or RAILWAY_PROJECT_ID)')
    ap.add_argument('--environment', default=RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT, help='Railway environment id (or RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT_ID)')
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if not args.project or not args.environment:
        sys.exit('set --project and --environment (or RAILWAY_PROJECT_ID / RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT_ID)')
    RAILWAY_PROJECT, RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT = args.project, args.environment

    ids = railway_services()
    wanted = args.only.split(',') if args.only else list(SERVICES)

    if args.write_keys:
        keys = {}
        for svc in SERVICES:
            names = railway_variables(ids[SERVICES[svc]], unrendered=True).keys()
            keys[svc] = sorted(k for k in names if not EXCLUDE.match(k))
        path = os.path.join(ENV_DIR, 'app-env-keys.json')
        with open(path, 'w') as f:
            json.dump(keys, f, indent=2)
            f.write('\n')
        print(f'wrote {path}; run terraform plan to see the task definition changes')
        return

    outputs = terraform_outputs()
    arns = outputs['app_secret_arns']
    rds_host = outputs['main_db_address']
    expected = json.load(open(os.path.join(ENV_DIR, 'app-env-keys.json')))

    for svc in wanted:
        values = railway_variables(ids[SERVICES[svc]])
        env = {k: v for k, v in values.items() if not EXCLUDE.match(k)}
        notes = []
        if 'DATABASE_URL' in env:
            env['DATABASE_URL'], note = rewrite_database_url(env['DATABASE_URL'], rds_host)
            notes.append(f'DATABASE_URL {note}')
        leftovers = sorted(k for k, v in env.items() if RAILWAY_HOSTS.search(v or ''))
        missing = sorted(set(expected.get(svc, [])) - set(env))
        extra = sorted(set(env) - set(expected.get(svc, [])))

        print(f'\n== {svc}: {len(env)} keys -> {arns[svc]}')
        for n in notes:
            print(f'   {n}')
        if leftovers:
            print(f'   WARNING still pointing at Railway: {leftovers}')
        if missing:
            print(f'   WARNING in app-env-keys.json but not on Railway (tasks will fail to start): {missing}')
        if extra:
            print(f'   NOTE on Railway but not in app-env-keys.json (not passed to the task): {extra}')

        if args.apply:
            with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile('w', delete=False, suffix='.json') as f:
                os.chmod(f.name, 0o600)
                json.dump(env, f)
            try:
                subprocess.run(['aws', 'secretsmanager', 'put-secret-value', '--secret-id', arns[svc],
                                '--secret-string', f'file://{f.name}', '--query', 'VersionId', '--output', 'text'], check=True)
            finally:
                os.unlink(f.name)

    if not args.apply:
        print('\ndry run: nothing written, rerun with --apply')

#!/bin/bash
# Decides which app images a deploy builds, which services it restarts and whether
# it runs prisma db push: Railway's per-service watch paths, with each app compared
# against the commit it runs now (the commit tag on its <app>-production image).
# Used by .github/workflows/deploy.yml; images come from docker/postiz-app.Dockerfile.
#
#   frontend       apps/frontend/**       -> service frontend
#   backend        apps/backend/**        -> services backend, mcp
#   orchestrator   apps/orchestrator/**   -> services worker, worker-2
#   every app      libraries/**, root build files, anything not listed as neutral
#   no app         docs, .github, apps/extension|sdk|commands, local dev files
#   prisma db push schema.prisma changed since the schema the database has: the
#                  commit on migrate-production, which only a successful push moves
#
# An app is built and restarted when something that touches it changed since its
# live commit, or when that is unclear: no live image yet, its commit is not an
# ancestor (rollback, rewritten history), or GitHub cannot list the diff (300+
# files). A re-run of the live commit restarts the app onto the existing image.
# libraries/** means every app: the workers import react-shared-libraries, and
# helpers is used everywhere. Manual runs build and restart everything.
#
# Environment: SHA, EVENT (github.event_name), APP_REPOSITORY, APP_TOKEN,
# REPOSITORY (ECR). Local checks: LIVE_FRONTEND / LIVE_BACKEND /
# LIVE_ORCHESTRATOR / LIVE_MIGRATE=<sha or empty> skip ECR, CHANGED_FILES (one
# path per line, used for every comparison) skips GitHub.
# Output: apps (JSON list), services (space-separated), db_push (true|false),
# to $GITHUB_OUTPUT when set, plus a summary for the run page.
set -euo pipefail
: "${SHA:?}"
APPS="frontend backend orchestrator"

services_of() {
  case $1 in
    frontend) echo frontend ;;
    backend) echo backend mcp ;;
    orchestrator) echo worker worker-2 ;;
  esac
}

# the commit an image tag runs: the <prefix><sha> tag next to it
live() { # tag prefix
  local var
  var="LIVE_$(echo "$1" | sed 's/-production$//' | tr 'a-z-' 'A-Z_')"
  if [ -n "${!var+x}" ]; then echo "${!var}"; return; fi
  aws ecr describe-images --repository-name "$REPOSITORY" --image-ids imageTag="$1" \
    --query 'imageDetails[0].imageTags' --output text 2>/dev/null \
    | tr '\t' '\n' | sed -n "s/^$2\([0-9a-f]\{40\}\)\$/\1/p" | head -1 || true
}

# files changed from a base commit to SHA; fails when that is unclear
changed() { # base
  if [ -n "${CHANGED_FILES+x}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$CHANGED_FILES"; return 0; fi
  local cmp status
  cmp=$(curl -fsSL -H "Authorization: Bearer $APP_TOKEN" -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github+json' \
    "https://api.github.com/repos/$APP_REPOSITORY/compare/$1...$SHA") || return 1
  status=$(jq -r .status <<< "$cmp")
  case $status in ahead | identical) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
  [ "$(jq '.files | length' <<< "$cmp")" -lt 300 ] || return 1
  jq -r '.files[] | .filename, (.previous_filename // empty)' <<< "$cmp"
}

touches() { # file -> the app it touches, "all", or nothing
  case $1 in
    apps/frontend/*) echo frontend ;;
    apps/backend/*) echo backend ;;
    apps/orchestrator/*) echo orchestrator ;;
    *.md | .github/* | apps/extension/* | apps/sdk/* | apps/commands/* | Jenkins/* | reports/* | .claude/* | .devcontainer/* \
      | docker-compose*.yaml | Dockerfile.dev | railway.toml | .coderabbit.yaml | sonar-project.properties | .env.example) ;;
    *) echo all ;;
  esac
}

apps="" services="" db_push=false why=""
note() { why="$why"$'\n'"- $1"; }

if [ -z "${CHANGED_FILES+x}" ] && [ "${EVENT:-}" != repository_dispatch ]; then
  apps="$APPS" db_push=true
  note "manual run: every app"
else
  : "${APP_REPOSITORY:=}" "${APP_TOKEN:=}" "${REPOSITORY:=}"
  for app in $APPS; do
    base=$(live "$app-production" "$app-")
    if [ -z "$base" ]; then apps="$apps $app"; note "$app: no live image yet"; continue; fi
    if [ "$base" = "$SHA" ]; then apps="$apps $app"; note "$app: already on ${SHA:0:12}, restarting it"; continue; fi
    if ! files=$(changed "$base"); then apps="$apps $app"; note "$app: cannot compare ${base:0:12}...${SHA:0:12}"; continue; fi
    hit=""
    while IFS= read -r f; do
      [ -n "$f" ] || continue
      t=$(touches "$f")
      if [ "$t" = all ] || [ "$t" = "$app" ]; then hit=$f; break; fi
    done <<< "$files"
    if [ -n "$hit" ]; then apps="$apps $app"; note "$app: changed since ${base:0:12} ($hit)"
    else note "$app: unchanged since ${base:0:12}"; fi
  done
  base=$(live migrate-production migrate-)
  if [ -z "$base" ]; then db_push=true; note "db push: no schema pushed by this pipeline yet"
  elif [ "$base" = "$SHA" ]; then note "db push: schema of ${SHA:0:12} already pushed"
  elif ! files=$(changed "$base"); then db_push=true; note "db push: cannot compare ${base:0:12}...${SHA:0:12}"
  elif grep -qxE 'libraries/nestjs-libraries/src/database/prisma/schema\.prisma' <<< "$files"; then
    db_push=true; note "db push: schema.prisma changed since ${base:0:12}"
  else note "db push: schema unchanged since ${base:0:12}"; fi
fi

for app in $apps; do services="$services $(services_of "$app")"; done
apps=$(echo $apps)
services=$(echo $services)
build=$apps
if [ "$db_push" = true ]; then build="$build migrate"; fi
json=$(printf '%s\n' $build | jq -Rsc 'split("\n") | map(select(length > 0))')

echo "apps=$json"
echo "services=$services"
echo "db_push=$db_push"
echo "why:${why}"
if [ -n "${GITHUB_OUTPUT:-}" ]; then printf 'apps=%s\nservices=%s\ndb_push=%s\n' "$json" "$services" "$db_push" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
if [ -n "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-}" ]; then
  printf '### Deploy plan for %s\n- builds: `%s`\n- restarts: `%s`\n- prisma db push: %s\n%s\n' \
    "${SHA:0:12}" "${json}" "${services:-nothing}" "$db_push" "$why" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
fi

# postiz-aws

The infrastructure behind [Postiz](https://github.com/gitroomhq/postiz-app)'s
hosted service on AWS, as Terraform, in the open like the app itself. It also
works as a reference for running Postiz on AWS yourself; see
[Running your own](#running-your-own).

It moves the Postiz and Temporal services from Railway to AWS (us-east-2).
Cloudflare R2 (media) and RunPod (media processing) stay where they are.

- Migration steps: [docs/migration-runbook.md](docs/migration-runbook.md)
- License: [AGPL-3.0](LICENSE), like Postiz

## What runs where

```
                     Cloudflare DNS (DNS-only records)
             api / mcp                      platform (the app)
                 |                                 |
                 |                       CloudFront (caches /_next/static)
                 v                                 |
     ALB (public subnets, TLS, host-based rules) <-+
        |                    |
        | instance targets   |
        v                    v
  ECS hosts: 2-4 x r8g.xlarge (Graviton, public subnets, no NAT gateway)
   bridge mode, egress via the host's public IP:
     backend x2 (autoscales to 4) . mcp . frontend x2 . worker . worker-2
   awsvpc mode, private subnets, Cloud Map postiz.internal:
     temporal-frontend x2 . temporal-history x2 . temporal-matching x2 . temporal-worker
     temporal-ui + Caddy basic auth (public, on an unlisted hostname like Railway's)

  db.r8g.large Multi-AZ,     2 x cache.t4g.micro,      1 x r8g.medium + EBS,
```

| Railway | AWS |
|---|---|
| Backend Postiz (2), MCP, Frontend, Worker, Worker 2 | ECS services with the same start commands, one image built from postiz-app |

| Redis | ElastiCache Valkey 8.1 (cluster mode off: Postiz uses a plain ioredis client, which Serverless does not accept) |

### Decisions worth knowing

- **No NAT gateway.** Most of what these services send leaves AWS: uploads
  relayed to R2, social APIs, RunPod. A NAT gateway would add $0.045 to every one
  of those GB, so the internet-facing containers run in bridge mode on hosts with
  public IPs. The hosts' security group only admits the ALB.
- **Workers cannot starve the API of connections.** Each process has a fixed
  pool: Prisma 8 (`connection_limit=8`), plus Mastra's pool in backend and MCP.
  On top of that, Postgres caps every role: `worker` 64, `mcp` 100, `temporal`
  400, `api` uncapped. The caps are set by `migrate-postgres.sh`; re-apply them
  with `migrate-postgres.sh connection-limits` (e.g. `WORKER_CONNECTIONS=128`
  before running more than 8 worker tasks). An alarm fires above 1000 connections
  in total (db.r8g.large allows ~1700). On Railway, PgBouncer's per-user pools did
  this; it ran in session mode, so it never shared connections, and is not needed here.
- **Temporal moves as an exact copy.** Same server build (pinned by digest),
  same schema and shard count, both stores frozen at the same moment, workers
  started only at go-live. The scripts refuse to copy otherwise. See
  [the checklist](docs/migration-runbook.md#temporal-what-keeps-the-workflows-intact).
- **Elasticsearch stays for now.** Postiz finds a post's running workflow with
  `workflow.list('postId="..." AND ExecutionStatus="Running"')` before deleting or
  rescheduling it. Switching an existing cluster to Postgres visibility hides every
  workflow that is already running, and `tdbg workflow refresh-tasks` does not
  rebuild them on 1.28 (tested). A deleted post could still publish. Amazon
  OpenSearch needs Temporal >= 1.30.1, so that is the follow-up after upgrading.
- **No secret in code or state.** Generated passwords (RDS admin, Valkey AUTH,
  Elasticsearch, the `temporal` role) are ephemeral values written write-only into
  the resource and a `postiz/production/managed/*` secret. App secrets are copied
  into Secrets Manager by a script; Terraform only knows their key names.
- **One database instance.** Both databases are light, so they share one
  Multi-AZ db.r8g.large: cheaper than a second instance, and
  Temporal gets Multi-AZ failover. If they ever compete (FreeableMemory,
  ReadIOPS), move `temporal` back out.
- **Temporal survives losing a host.** Frontend, history and matching run two
  tasks each on different hosts. The rehearsal stopped one history task: new and
  existing workflows kept working.
- **Hosts patch themselves.** Each host is replaced every 14 days with the newest
  ECS-optimized AMI (SSM-resolved), and tasks are drained first.

### Running this as a public repository

- Pull requests from forks never get AWS credentials: GitHub gives no OIDC token to fork PRs, and the roles trust only this repository's pull requests and `main` (plan, read-only), the `production` environment (apply) and the `deploy` environment (deploys).
- Turn on *Settings > Actions > Require approval for all outside collaborators*, and restrict both environments to the `main` branch. Every push to `main` applies with the admin role, so write access to this repository means admin on the AWS account: keep it to the people who run production, or add required reviewers to `production`.
- Actions logs of a public repository are public. They contain plans and deploy output (resource IDs, private hostnames), never secret values. The account id is a secret, so the logs print `***` for it, also inside ARNs and the ECR registry name; the alert emails are a secret and a sensitive Terraform variable. PR comments carry only the plan's summary line.
- Automatic deploys only ship commits on the app's `main`: **deploy-postiz** checks a dispatched commit against the app repository before it builds anything, so a leaked dispatch token cannot deploy a branch or a fork's pull request.
- The Temporal UI is public like on Railway, behind basic auth, on an unlisted hostname: a random name kept in the `TEMPORAL_UI_DOMAIN` secret and covered by a wildcard certificate, so it shows up neither in this repository, nor in the logs, nor in certificate transparency logs. `temporal_ui_allowed_cidrs` can limit it to a few IP ranges. Forks can keep the variable's default, `temporal_ui_public = false`: no public hostname at all, `scripts/temporal-ui-tunnel.sh` opens it through Session Manager.

## Day to day

**Infrastructure changes:** open a PR to see the plan first: CI runs fmt,
validate, the offline test and a plan (summary commented on the PR). Every push
to `main` that touches `environments/` or `modules/` applies right away, merges
included, and a local apply that never reaches `main` is undone by the next
push. PR plans run with `-refresh=false`, because the
plan role cannot read any secret value. Do the same when planning with the
read-only profile.

```bash
terraform -chdir=environments/production init -backend=false && terraform -chdir=environments/production test   # offline, no credentials
```

**Deploy Postiz:** pushing to postiz-app `main` deploys it, like on Railway.
postiz-app's `.github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml` sends a `repository_dispatch` to
this repo's **deploy-postiz** workflow. It skips commits that only touch docs,
the extension, the SDK or CI. One-time setup:

1. Create a fine-grained token with *Contents: read and write* on this repository only.
2. Save it in postiz-app as the secret `POSTIZ_AWS_DISPATCH_TOKEN`.
3. Set the variable `AUTO_DEPLOY = true` in this repo at the cutover. Until then dispatches are ignored, because `prisma db push` must not touch the empty database before the restore.

postiz-app's trigger skips commits that change no file outside the ignored paths,
so an empty commit (`git commit --allow-empty`) never deploys: test with a real
one-line change.

**One slim image per app, built only when the app changed**
(`docker/postiz-app.Dockerfile`; postiz-app's own all-in-one image stays the
self-hosting path and is not changed):

| Image | Services | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `frontend-<sha>` | frontend | Next standalone server (switched on by a config wrapper at build time) |
| `backend-<sha>` | backend, mcp | the backend build and only the files `main.js` loads (traced with `@vercel/nft`) |
| `orchestrator-<sha>` | worker, worker-2 | the same for the workers, plus every file Temporal's workflow bundler reads at startup |
| `migrate-<sha>` | db push task | Prisma CLI and `schema.prisma` |

The **deploy-postiz** run has three jobs. **plan** (`scripts/deploy-plan.sh`)
compares each app with the commit it runs now, the `<app>-<sha>` tag next to its
`<app>-production` tag: `apps/frontend` touches the frontend, `apps/backend` the
backend (and mcp), `apps/orchestrator` the workers, and `libraries/**` or the root
build files every app. **build** builds only those images, in parallel, one job
each, and reuses an image already pushed for the commit. **release** runs
`prisma db push` when `schema.prisma` changed since the schema the database has
(the commit on `migrate-production`, which only a successful push moves), moves
`<app>-production` and restarts only those
services. Anything unclear (no live image, a rollback, rewritten history, a huge
diff) builds and restarts that app; every manual run does all of them. The run's
summary shows the plan and why.

You can also run **deploy-postiz** by hand with any ref. It builds `linux/arm64`
and runs the db push as a one-off task (Railway's pre-deploy command), and only
moves the release tags and rolls the services if that succeeds. A failed rollout
is rolled back by the ECS circuit breaker; after a failed db push the next deploy
pushes again. Pushes that land while a deploy runs
collapse into one deploy of the newest commit. To roll back a release, run
**deploy-postiz** with the previous commit and `skip_db_push` checked. Its images
are reused when they exist, and `prisma db push` would refuse to drop columns the
newer release added.

**A new version only takes over once it is healthy.** Deploys are rolling:
ECS starts the new tasks next to the old ones and stops an old task only after
its replacement passes its check:

- **backend, mcp:** load balancer `GET /` (200 "App is running!").
- **frontend:** load balancer `GET /favicon.ico`.
- **worker, worker-2:** the orchestrator's own `/health/status` on port 3002, which answers 200 only once it reaches Temporal.
- **temporal-frontend:** `temporal operator cluster health`.
- **temporal-ui:** Caddy `GET /healthz` as a container check (and through the load balancer when public).

The load balancer sends traffic to a new task after 2 passing checks (15 s
apart), and old tasks get 120 s to finish in-flight uploads. If new tasks keep
failing (3 times for a 1-task service), the circuit breaker rolls the service
back to the previous revision. That includes the previous image digest, even
though `<app>-production` moved. The deploy workflow fails if services are not
stable within 30 minutes.

**Schema changes run once per deploy:** the `db-push` one-off task, started by
**deploy-postiz** and awaited before the rollout. The services only start their
app (`node .../main.js`, `node server.js`, the image's own command): unlike the
self-hosted image, a container start never touches the schema. Temporal's own schema check runs when a `temporal-frontend` task
starts, but it changes nothing unless `temporal_image` moved to a newer release.
For that upgrade, set `temporal_task_counts.frontend = 1` for the apply (so one
task migrates), then back to 2.

**Temporal UI:** `terraform -chdir=environments/production output -raw temporal_ui_url`,
behind basic auth with the user and password from `postiz/production/temporal-ui-auth`
(the same as on Railway). With `temporal_ui_public = false` it has no public
hostname, and `scripts/temporal-ui-tunnel.sh` opens it on http://localhost:8081
through Session Manager (needs the [Session Manager plugin](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/session-manager-working-with-install-plugin.html)).

**Change an environment variable:**

1. Edit the value in Secrets Manager (`postiz/production/<service>`).
2. If the key is new, add its name to `environments/production/app-env-keys.json`, or regenerate the file with `scripts/railway-env-to-secrets.py --write-keys` (with `RAILWAY_PROJECT_ID` and `RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT_ID` set) while Railway is still the source.
3. Apply.
4. Running tasks keep old values until they restart: roll the service with **deploy-postiz**, or run `aws ecs update-service --force-new-deployment`.

**Shell into a container:**

```bash
aws ecs execute-command --cluster postiz-production --task <task-id> --container backend --interactive --command sh
```

**Rotate a generated password:** bump `main_db_password_version` or
`redis_auth_token_version` and apply. The resource and its secret change
together. Then restart the services that read it: backend, mcp, worker and
worker-2 for Valkey; nothing reads the main admin password at runtime.

The `temporal` role is created by the migration script, so Terraform cannot
change its password. Bump `temporal_db_password_version`, apply, run
`migrate-postgres.sh temporal-password` in the ops task, then restart the
`temporal-*` services.

Elasticsearch stores its password in its own data. After bumping
`elasticsearch_password_version`, open a Session Manager shell on the host, run
`rotate-elastic-password`, then restart the `temporal-*` services.

**Read-only access for AI agents:**

```ini
# ~/.aws/config
[profile postiz-readonly]
role_arn = arn:aws:iam::<account id>:role/postiz-agent-readonly
source_profile = <your admin profile>
region = us-east-2
```

It is `ReadOnlyAccess` plus Terraform state, with secret values,
`ecs:ExecuteCommand` and Session Manager denied.

## Running your own

The modules are generic; `environments/production` is Postiz's own setup.

1. Fork, change `github_repository`, `github_oidc_subject` (printed by `gh api repos/<owner>/<name>/actions/oidc/customization/sub --jq .sub_claim_prefix`), the domains, sizes and region in `environments/production/terraform.tfvars`, and set the secrets, variables and environments above (`bootstrap/` takes the same two from `TF_VAR_github_repository` and `TF_VAR_github_oidc_subject`).
2. Follow phase A of the runbook. The Railway-specific steps (copying env vars and data) are optional. For a new installation, fill the Secrets Manager secrets by hand, then in the ops task (runbook B1) run `migrate-postgres.sh init`: it creates the app roles with the passwords of the backend, mcp and worker `DATABASE_URL`s, and the `temporal` database. The first **deploy-postiz** run creates the tables, and Temporal sets up its own schema on start.
3. Your organization may allow different regions; ACM certificates for CloudFront always live in us-east-1.

## Not in this repo yet

The other services Postiz runs on Railway (side apps, automation, the CMS,
monitoring) and a staging environment. `modules/ecs-service` is meant for them:
most are one more `module` block plus a secret.

#!/bin/bash
# Move a Railway PostgreSQL database into RDS, see docs/migration-runbook.md.
#
# The runbook's way opens no port anywhere: export runs in a temporary service
# inside the Railway project, import in the AWS ops task (docker/ops.Dockerfile),
# and scripts/migration-transfer.sh carries the files between them through the
# private migration bucket. copy does both on one machine that reaches both sides.
#
#   migrate-postgres.sh preflight main|temporal       read-only report of the side(s) this machine
#                                                     reaches (SOURCE_URL, MAIN_ADMIN_URL)
#   migrate-postgres.sh export    main|temporal DIR   source side: dump, extensions, row counts and,
#                                                     for main, the app roles' password verifiers into DIR
#   migrate-postgres.sh import    main|temporal DIR   AWS side: roles, restore DIR, fix up, verify the
#                                                     row counts the export recorded
#   migrate-postgres.sh copy      main|temporal       export to $WORK and import, in one go
#   migrate-postgres.sh temporal-password             set the temporal role to the current secret
#                                                     (after bumping temporal_db_password_version)
#   migrate-postgres.sh connection-limits             re-apply the per-role connection caps below
#   migrate-postgres.sh init                          no data from Railway (new installation, test run):
#                                                     create the roles and the temporal database, each
#                                                     role with the password of the app DATABASE_URL the
#                                                     ops task injects (API_/MCP_/WORKER_DATABASE_URL),
#                                                     or of API_DB_PASSWORD, MCP_DB_PASSWORD, WORKER_DB_PASSWORD
#   migrate-postgres.sh reset                         empty postiz, temporal and the Temporal search index
#                                                     on AWS, keeping the logins (around the test run on
#                                                     empty databases); refuses while anything is connected
#
# Both databases live on the one RDS instance:
#   main      Railway "Postgres"      -> database postiz,   owned by "api"
#   temporal  Railway "Postgres-NlPS" -> database temporal, owned by "temporal"
#
# Environment:
#   SOURCE_URL            the source database as the postgres superuser (preflight, export, copy;
#                         on Railway the service's DATABASE_URL, migration-transfer.sh sets it)
#   MAIN_ADMIN_URL        injected by the ops task (RDS master user, database postiz)
#   TEMPORAL_DB_PASSWORD  injected by the ops task (Terraform-generated login of "temporal")
#   TARGET_ES_URL         injected by the ops task (reset deletes the Temporal index there)
#   ES_INDEX              Temporal visibility index, default temporal_visibility_v1_dev
#   JOBS                  parallel dump/restore workers, default 8
#   WORK                  where copy keeps its dump, default /work
#   APP_ROLES             login roles the apps use on postiz, default "api mcp worker"
#   NUM_HISTORY_SHARDS    expected Temporal shard count, default 4 (Terraform temporal_num_history_shards)
#   TEMPORAL_SCHEMA       expected Temporal schema version, default 1.17 (what auto-setup 1.28.0 runs)
#   FORCE=1               turn the safety stops below into warnings (rehearsals while Railway runs)
#   WORKER_CONNECTIONS    cap for the worker role, default 64 (8 per process: up to 8 worker tasks)
#   MCP_CONNECTIONS       cap for the mcp role, default 100 (Prisma 8 + Mastra's pool per task)
#   TEMPORAL_CONNECTIONS  cap for the temporal role, default 400 (20 per Temporal task, deploys double them)
#
# Per-role caps: Postgres refuses a role's connection beyond its cap, so a
# runaway worker or Temporal can never take connections the API (role api,
# uncapped) or MCP need. On Railway, PgBouncer's per-user pools did this.
#
# Safety stops: nothing else may be connected to the source (preflight, export),
# because a copy taken while Temporal or the apps still write is silently stale;
# for temporal, the shard count and schema version must be the ones the AWS
# cluster runs, so the restored history is served by the same Temporal release;
# and the restored row counts must be the ones recorded at export (import).
#
# Ownership: RDS has no superuser, so instead of copying Railway's role flags,
# "api" owns every object in postiz and "mcp"/"worker" log in with their own
# passwords but act as "api" (ALTER ROLE ... SET role). Whatever the services
# create later (prisma db push, Mastra tables) is owned by "api", the role
# prisma db push runs as. Everything in temporal is owned by "temporal".
set -euo pipefail

mode=${1:-}
target=${2:-}
dir=${3:-}
JOBS=${JOBS:-8}
APP_ROLES=${APP_ROLES:-"api mcp worker"}
ADMIN_URL=${MAIN_ADMIN_URL:-}

usage() {
  echo "usage: $0 preflight|copy main|temporal  |  $0 export|import main|temporal DIR  |  $0 init  |  $0 reset  |  $0 temporal-password  |  $0 connection-limits" >&2
  exit 2
}

need_admin() {
  [ -n "$ADMIN_URL" ] || { echo "MAIN_ADMIN_URL missing, run this inside the ops task" >&2; exit 1; }
}

need_source() {
  [ -n "${SOURCE_URL:-}" ] || { echo "set SOURCE_URL to the source database, as the postgres superuser (on Railway its DATABASE_URL)" >&2; exit 1; }
}

need_temporal_password() {
  : "${TEMPORAL_DB_PASSWORD:[REDACTED] missing, run this inside the ops task}"
}

admin() { psql "$ADMIN_URL" -X -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 "$@"; }
src() { psql "$SOURCE_URL" -X -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 "$@"; }
dst() { psql "$TARGET_URL" -X -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 "$@"; }

# the admin URL with another database name swapped in
admin_url_for() {
  python3 -c 'import sys; from urllib.parse import urlsplit, urlunsplit; u = urlsplit(sys.argv[1]); print(urlunsplit(u._replace(path="/" + sys.argv[2])))' "$ADMIN_URL" "$1"
}

stop_unless_forced() {
  if [ "${FORCE:-0}" = 1 ]; then
    echo "WARNING (FORCE=1): $*" >&2
  else
    echo "STOP: $*" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

# other clients' sessions; autovacuum and other background workers do not count
OTHERS="from pg_stat_activity where datname = current_database() and pid <> pg_backend_pid() and backend_type = 'client backend'"

# exact row count of every table, one query per side
COUNT_SQL="select table_schema || '.' || table_name,
  (xpath('/row/c/text()', query_to_xml(format('select count(*) as c from %I.%I', table_schema, table_name), false, true, '')))[1]::text
  from information_schema.tables
  where table_type = 'BASE TABLE' and table_schema not in ('pg_catalog', 'information_schema')
  order by 1"

# The app roles' caps. temporal's is set with its role (prepare_temporal): the
# main and temporal imports run at the same time, and two sessions altering one
# role at once fail with "tuple concurrently updated".
app_connection_limits() {
  admin -q <<SQL
alter role worker connection limit ${WORKER_CONNECTIONS:-64};
alter role mcp connection limit ${MCP_CONNECTIONS:-100};
SQL
}

connection_limits() {
  app_connection_limits
  if [ -n "$(admin -Atc "select 1 from pg_roles where rolname = 'temporal'")" ]; then
    admin -qc "alter role temporal connection limit ${TEMPORAL_CONNECTIONS:-400}"
  fi
  admin -c "select rolname, rolconnlimit as connection_limit from pg_roles where rolname in ('api', 'mcp', 'worker', 'temporal') order by 1"
}

preflight_source() {
  echo "== source"
  src -c "select current_database() as db, pg_size_pretty(pg_database_size(current_database())) as size, current_setting('server_version') as version"
  src -c "select rolname, rolsuper, rolcreaterole, rolcreatedb, rolcanlogin, rolbypassrls from pg_roles where rolname !~ '^pg_' order by 1"
  src -c "select n.nspname as schema, pg_get_userbyid(c.relowner) as owner, count(*) as objects
          from pg_class c join pg_namespace n on n.oid = c.relnamespace
          where n.nspname not in ('pg_catalog', 'information_schema', 'pg_toast') group by 1, 2 order by 1, 2"
  src -c "select extname, extversion from pg_extension order by 1"
  if [ "$target" = temporal ]; then
    src -c "select db_name, curr_version from schema_version"
    src -c "select count(*) as history_shards from shards"
    src -c "select count(*) as running_workflows from current_executions where status = 1"
  fi

  echo "== safety checks"
  others=$(src -Atc "select count(*) $OTHERS")
  if [ "$others" != 0 ]; then
    src -c "select usename, application_name, client_addr, state $OTHERS"
    stop_unless_forced "$others other connections to the source. Stop every writer first (apps, workers, PgBouncer, the four Temporal services, anything else using this database)"
  else
    echo "no other connections to the source: writers are stopped"
  fi
  if [ "$target" = temporal ]; then
    shards=$(src -Atc "select count(*) from shards")
    [ "$shards" = "${NUM_HISTORY_SHARDS:-4}" ] || stop_unless_forced "source has $shards history shards, the AWS cluster is configured for ${NUM_HISTORY_SHARDS:-4} (temporal_num_history_shards)"
    version=$(src -Atc "select curr_version from schema_version limit 1")
    [ "$version" = "${TEMPORAL_SCHEMA:-1.17}" ] || stop_unless_forced "source schema is $version, expected ${TEMPORAL_SCHEMA:-1.17}: Railway is not running the Temporal release AWS will run"
    echo "shards $shards and schema $version match the AWS cluster"
  fi
}

preflight_target() {
  echo "== target ($DB)"
  admin -c "select current_setting('server_version') as version"
  if [ -n "$(admin -Atc "select 1 from pg_database where datname = '$DB'")" ]; then
    n=$(dst -Atc "select count(*) from pg_tables where schemaname not in ('pg_catalog', 'information_schema')")
    if [ "$n" != 0 ]; then
      echo "database $DB already has $n tables: restore into an empty database only (migrate-postgres.sh reset)" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "database $DB exists and is empty"
  else
    echo "database $DB does not exist yet, import creates it"
  fi
}

prepare_main() {
  local sql
  sql=$(mktemp)
  chmod 600 "$sql"
  {
    echo "set createrole_self_grant = 'set, inherit';"
    for role in $APP_ROLES; do
      if [ "$mode" = init ]; then
        # no source: the password from <ROLE>_DB_PASSWORD, else from <ROLE>_DATABASE_URL
        # when that URL logs in as this role, so the apps' DATABASE_URLs work as they are
        var="$(echo "$role" | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]')_DB_PASSWORD"
        url_var="$(echo "$role" | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]')_DATABASE_URL"
        hash="${!var:-}"
        if [ -z "$hash" ] && [ -n "${!url_var:-}" ]; then
          hash=$(python3 -c 'import sys; from urllib.parse import urlsplit, unquote; u = urlsplit(sys.argv[1]); print(unquote(u.password or "") if u.username == sys.argv[2] else "")' "${!url_var}" "$role")
        fi
        if [ -z "$hash" ]; then echo "set $var, or $url_var to a URL that logs in as $role" >&2; exit 1; fi
      else
        # same password verifier as on Railway, so the DATABASE_URLs keep working
        hash=$(awk -F '\t' -v role="$role" '$1 == role { print $2 }' "$dir/roles")
        if [ -z "$hash" ]; then echo "role $role missing from $dir/roles" >&2; exit 1; fi
      fi
      hash=${hash//\'/\'\'}
      echo "do \$\$ begin if not exists (select from pg_roles where rolname = '$role') then create role \"$role\" login; end if; end \$\$;"
      # only LOGIN + password: superuser flags cannot be set on RDS, new roles have none
      echo "alter role \"$role\" with login password '$hash';"
    done
    echo "grant connect, create, temporary on database \"$DB\" to \"$OWNER_ROLE\";"
    echo "grant all on schema public to \"$OWNER_ROLE\";"
    for role in $APP_ROLES; do
      [ "$role" = "$OWNER_ROLE" ] && continue
      echo "grant \"$OWNER_ROLE\" to \"$role\";"
      echo "alter role \"$role\" set role = '$OWNER_ROLE';"
    done
  } > "$sql"
  dst -q -f "$sql"
  rm -f "$sql"
  app_connection_limits
  echo "roles ready: $APP_ROLES (owner: $OWNER_ROLE)"
}

prepare_temporal() {
  admin -q <<SQL
set createrole_self_grant = 'set, inherit';
do \$\$ begin if not exists (select from pg_roles where rolname = 'temporal') then create role temporal login; end if; end \$\$;
alter role temporal with login password '$TEMPORAL_DB_PASSWORD';
SQL
  if [ -z "$(admin -Atc "select 1 from pg_database where datname = 'temporal'")" ]; then
    admin -qc "create database temporal owner temporal"
  fi
  admin -qc "alter role temporal connection limit ${TEMPORAL_CONNECTIONS:-400}"
  echo "role temporal and database temporal ready"
}

# source side: everything import needs, into $dir
dump_source() {
  if [ -e "$dir" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$dir")" ]; then
    echo "$dir is not empty: export into a new directory" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  preflight_source
  mkdir -p "$dir"
  src -Atc "select extname from pg_extension where extname <> 'plpgsql' order by 1" > "$dir/extensions"
  if [ "$target" = main ]; then
    # the app roles' password verifiers, not the passwords
    (
      umask 077
      for role in $APP_ROLES; do
        hash=$(src -Atc "select rolpassword from pg_authid where rolname = '$role'")
        if [ -z "$hash" ]; then echo "role $role not found on the source" >&2; exit 1; fi
        printf '%s\t%s\n' "$role" "$hash"
      done > "$dir/roles"
    )
  fi

  echo "== dump ($JOBS jobs)"
  time pg_dump "$SOURCE_URL" --format=directory --jobs="$JOBS" --no-owner --no-privileges --compress=3 --file="$dir/dump"
  du -sh "$dir/dump"

  echo "== row counts"
  if [ "$target" = temporal ]; then
    src -Atc "select count(*) from current_executions where status = 1" > "$dir/running-workflows"
  fi
  # written last and in one step: an export without source-counts is incomplete
  src -AtF $'\t' -c "$COUNT_SQL" > "$dir/source-counts.tmp"
  mv "$dir/source-counts.tmp" "$dir/source-counts"
  echo "exported $(wc -l < "$dir/source-counts") tables to $dir"
}

# AWS side: restore what dump_source wrote into $dir
restore_export() {
  if [ ! -d "$dir/dump" ] || [ ! -f "$dir/source-counts" ]; then
    echo "$dir is not a complete export (migrate-postgres.sh export)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  preflight_target
  if [ "$target" = main ]; then prepare_main; else prepare_temporal; fi
  # pg_restore would create them as the restoring role; some need rds_superuser
  for ext in $(cat "$dir/extensions"); do
    dst -qc "create extension if not exists \"$ext\""
    echo "extension $ext"
  done

  echo "== restore as $OWNER_ROLE ($JOBS jobs)"
  # extensions were created above by the admin user; the restoring role may not
  # own them (or the public schema), so their entries and comments are skipped
  pg_restore --list "$dir/dump" | grep -v -E ' EXTENSION - | COMMENT - EXTENSION | COMMENT - SCHEMA public ' > "$dir/restore.toc"
  set +e
  time pg_restore --dbname="$TARGET_URL" --jobs="$JOBS" --no-owner --no-privileges --role="$OWNER_ROLE" \
    --use-list="$dir/restore.toc" "$dir/dump" 2> "$dir/restore.log"
  status=$?
  set -e
  if [ $status -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "pg_restore reported errors (full log: $dir/restore.log):" >&2
    grep -i error "$dir/restore.log" | head -30 >&2
  fi

  if [ "$target" = temporal ]; then
    # Temporal keys its schema version row by database name (Railway: "railway").
    # Without this, auto-setup re-runs every migration and the frontend crash-loops.
    dst -c "update schema_version set db_name = current_database() where db_name <> current_database() returning db_name, curr_version"
    running_src=$(cat "$dir/running-workflows")
    running_dst=$(dst -Atc "select count(*) from current_executions where status = 1")
    if [ "$running_src" = "$running_dst" ]; then
      echo "running workflows: $running_dst, as exported"
    else
      stop_unless_forced "running workflows differ: exported $running_src, restored $running_dst"
    fi
  fi

  echo "== analyze"
  dst -qc "set client_min_messages = error; analyze"

  echo "== verify row counts"
  dst -AtF $'\t' -c "$COUNT_SQL" > "$dir/target-counts"
  if diff "$dir/source-counts" "$dir/target-counts" > "$dir/count-diff"; then
    echo "OK: $(wc -l < "$dir/source-counts") tables, identical row counts"
  else
    echo "ROW COUNT MISMATCH (export < > restored):" >&2
    cat "$dir/count-diff" >&2
    stop_unless_forced "the restored row counts differ from the export"
  fi
  [ $status -eq 0 ] || { echo "pg_restore logged errors, read $dir/restore.log before going on" >&2; exit 1; }
}

copy() {
  preflight_target # the target must be empty before a long dump
  dir="${WORK:-/work}/${target}-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
  dump_source
  restore_export
}

# new installation without Railway: roles and the temporal database, no data;
# the db-push task then creates the postiz tables and Temporal its schema
init() {
  prepare_main
  prepare_temporal
  echo "ready: set each service's DATABASE_URL to postgresql://<role>:<password>@<host>:5432/postiz?connection_limit=8&application_name=<role>"
}

# Back to empty databases for the test run, or after it, before the real copy.
# The roles and their passwords stay, so the apps' DATABASE_URLs keep working;
# prisma db push recreates the tables, Temporal's auto-setup its schema and index.
reset() {
  local maint others answer
  maint=$(admin_url_for postgres)
  others=$(psql "$maint" -X -Atc "select count(*) from pg_stat_activity where datname in ('$DB', 'temporal') and backend_type = 'client backend'")
  if [ "$others" != 0 ]; then
    psql "$maint" -X -c "select datname, usename, application_name, client_addr from pg_stat_activity where datname in ('$DB', 'temporal') and backend_type = 'client backend'"
    # no FORCE here: a connection means an app, Temporal or a db push still uses these databases
    echo "STOP: $others connections to $DB/temporal. Set apps_enabled = false, push, and wait until every service runs 0 tasks" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  read -r -p "This deletes all data in $DB, temporal and the $ES_INDEX index on AWS. Type reset to continue: " answer || true
  [ "$answer" = reset ] || { echo "nothing changed" >&2; exit 1; }

  # no FORCE: DROP DATABASE stops autovacuum workers by itself, while FORCE fails for
  # a non-superuser master when one runs ("permission denied to terminate process")
  psql "$maint" -X -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -q \
    -c "drop database if exists \"$DB\"" -c "create database \"$DB\"" \
    -c 'drop database if exists temporal'
  # the same grants an import sets up: prisma db push runs as the owner role
  dst -q <<SQL
grant connect, create, temporary on database "$DB" to "$OWNER_ROLE";
grant all on schema public to "$OWNER_ROLE";
SQL
  prepare_temporal
  curl -fsS -X DELETE "$TARGET_ES_URL/$ES_INDEX?ignore_unavailable=true" > /dev/null
  echo "empty: $DB, temporal and $ES_INDEX; logins kept"
}

case "$mode:$target" in
  connection-limits: | temporal-password: | init: | reset:)
    DB=postiz
    OWNER_ROLE=$(echo "$APP_ROLES" | awk '{print $1}')
    ;;
  preflight:main | export:main | import:main | copy:main)
    DB=postiz
    OWNER_ROLE=$(echo "$APP_ROLES" | awk '{print $1}')
    ;;
  preflight:temporal | export:temporal | import:temporal | copy:temporal)
    DB=temporal
    OWNER_ROLE=temporal
    ;;
  *)
    usage
    ;;
esac

case "$mode" in
  preflight)
    [ -n "${SOURCE_URL:-}$ADMIN_URL" ] || { echo "set SOURCE_URL (source side), or run this inside the ops task (AWS side)" >&2; exit 1; }
    ;;
  export)
    need_source
    [ -n "$dir" ] || usage
    ;;
  import)
    need_admin
    [ -n "$dir" ] || usage
    [ "$target" = main ] || need_temporal_password
    ;;
  copy)
    need_source
    need_admin
    [ "$target" = main ] || need_temporal_password
    ;;
  reset)
    need_admin
    need_temporal_password
    : "[REDACTED] missing, run this inside the ops task}"
    ES_INDEX=${ES_INDEX:-temporal_visibility_v1_dev}
    ;;
  *)
    need_admin
    [ "$mode" = connection-limits ] || need_temporal_password
    ;;
esac
if [ -n "$ADMIN_URL" ]; then TARGET_URL=$(admin_url_for "$DB"); fi

case "$mode" in
  preflight)
    if [ -n "${SOURCE_URL:-}" ]; then preflight_source; fi
    if [ -n "$ADMIN_URL" ]; then preflight_target; fi
    ;;
  export) dump_source ;;
  import) restore_export ;;
  copy) copy ;;
  init) init ;;
  reset) reset ;;
  connection-limits) connection_limits ;;
  temporal-password)
    admin -qc "alter role temporal with login password '$TEMPORAL_DB_PASSWORD'"
    echo "temporal role now uses the current secret; restart the temporal-* services"
    ;;
esac

# Migration toolbox, for the ops ECS task and the temporary Railway toolbox that
# exports the data: PostgreSQL 16 client tools (same major as Railway and RDS),
# python3 for es-copy-index.py, the AWS CLI for the migration bucket, tmux so a
# long copy survives a dropped shell, and scripts/.
# Build context: this repository.
FROM postgres:16-bookworm

RUN apt-get update \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends python3 ca-certificates curl jq less procps awscli tmux \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

COPY scripts/ /opt/postiz/
# Linked into /usr/local/bin as well: tmux starts login shells, whose /etc/profile
# resets PATH as root and drops /opt/postiz. The scripts find their siblings
# through their own directory, so every script is linked.
RUN chmod +x /opt/postiz/* && ln -s /opt/postiz/* /usr/local/bin/
ENV PATH=/opt/postiz:$PATH
# ECS Exec sets no TERM, and tmux refuses to start without one
ENV TERM=xterm-256color

WORKDIR /work
CMD ["sleep", "86400"]

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7
#
# Postiz for ECS: one image for backend, MCP, frontend and both workers; the
# task definition picks the process (pnpm run start:prod:backend | frontend |
# orchestrator), the same commands Railway runs.
#
# Build context: a checkout of gitroomhq/postiz-app (see .github/workflows/deploy.yml).
# Node and pnpm versions follow its package.json (engines, packageManager).

# --- build -------------------------------------------------------------------------
FROM node:22.23.4-bookworm-slim AS build

RUN apt-get update \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends g++ make python3 ca-certificates openssl libudev-dev \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

RUN npm --no-update-notifier --no-fund --global install pnpm@10.6.1

WORKDIR /app

# Plain install, as on Railway: the root postinstall runs `pnpm dlx prisma`,
# which needs the network, so the `pnpm fetch` + offline-install split does not work.
COPY . /app
RUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

# NEXT_PUBLIC_* values are compiled into the browser bundle, so they must exist
# at build time (Railway passed the Frontend service variables to its build).
# They arrive as a BuildKit secret file of KEY='value' lines and never land in
# an image layer. NEXT_PUBLIC_VERSION stays unset: it marks self-hosted builds.
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=frontend_env,required=false \
    set -a \
 && if [ -f /run/secrets/frontend_env ]; then . /run/secrets/frontend_env; fi \
 && set +a \
 && NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=6144" pnpm run build

# --- runtime ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Same base, without the compiler toolchain and the pnpm store.
FROM node:22.23.4-bookworm-slim

# openssl: Prisma's query engine; libudev1: native USB/HID modules compiled above
RUN apt-get update \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates openssl libudev1 \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
 && npm --no-update-notifier --no-fund --global install pnpm@10.6.1

WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build /app /app

ENV NODE_ENV=production
CMD ["pnpm", "run", "start:prod:backend"]

#!/bin/bash
# Elasticsearch ${es_version} for Temporal visibility (secret version ${secret_version}, ${secret_resource}).
# Runs once at first boot. The password is read from Secrets Manager by the
# instance role at every start, so it never appears in user data.
set -euxo pipefail

# The data volume is attached after the instance boots; wait for it.
DEVICE=/dev/disk/by-id/nvme-Amazon_Elastic_Block_Store_${replace(volume_id, "-", "")}
for _ in $(seq 1 120); do
  [ -e "$DEVICE" ] && break
  sleep 5
done
[ -e "$DEVICE" ] || { echo "data volume ${volume_id} never attached" >&2; exit 1; }

# Format only a blank volume: a replaced host keeps the existing index.
if ! blkid "$DEVICE"; then
  mkfs.xfs "$DEVICE"
fi
mkdir -p /var/lib/elasticsearch
UUID=$(blkid -s UUID -o value "$DEVICE")
grep -q "$UUID" /etc/fstab || echo "UUID=$UUID /var/lib/elasticsearch xfs defaults,nofail 0 2" >> /etc/fstab
mount -a
chown -R 1000:0 /var/lib/elasticsearch

echo 'vm.max_map_count=262144' > /etc/sysctl.d/99-elasticsearch.conf
sysctl --system

dnf install -y docker
systemctl enable --now docker

# The host sits in a public subnet: publish 9200 on the private IP only, so the
# port stays closed to the internet even if the security group were opened.
TOKEN=$(curl -sX PUT http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token -H 'X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds: 60')
PRIVATE_IP=$(curl -s -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token: $TOKEN" http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/local-ipv4)
echo "PRIVATE_IP=$PRIVATE_IP" > /etc/elasticsearch.env

cat > /usr/local/bin/run-elasticsearch <<'SCRIPT'
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
. /etc/elasticsearch.env
PASSWORD=$(aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --region ${region} --secret-id ${secret_arn} \
  --query SecretString --output text | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["password"])')
docker rm -f elasticsearch >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
exec docker run --name elasticsearch --rm \
  -p "$PRIVATE_IP:9200:9200" \
  -v /var/lib/elasticsearch:/usr/share/elasticsearch/data \
  --ulimit nofile=65535:65535 --ulimit memlock=-1:-1 \
  -e discovery.type=single-node \
  -e node.name=elasticsearch \
  -e bootstrap.memory_lock=true \
  -e xpack.security.enabled=true \
  -e xpack.security.enrollment.enabled=false \
  -e xpack.security.http.ssl.enabled=false \
  -e xpack.security.transport.ssl.enabled=false \
  -e "ES_JAVA_OPTS=-Xms${es_heap} -Xmx${es_heap}" \
  -e "ELASTIC_PASSWORD=$PASSWORD" \
  --log-driver awslogs \
  --log-opt awslogs-region=${region} \
  --log-opt awslogs-group=${log_group} \
  --log-opt awslogs-stream=elasticsearch \
  docker.elastic.co/elasticsearch/elasticsearch:${es_version}
SCRIPT
chmod 700 /usr/local/bin/run-elasticsearch

# ELASTIC_PASSWORD only applies on the very first start. After bumping
# elasticsearch_password_version, run this on the host (Session Manager) to move
# the elastic user from the previous secret value to the current one, then
# restart the Temporal services.
cat > /usr/local/bin/rotate-elastic-password <<'SCRIPT'
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
. /etc/elasticsearch.env
get() {
  aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --region ${region} --secret-id ${secret_arn} --version-stage "$1" \
    --query SecretString --output text | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["password"])'
}
OLD=$(get AWSPREVIOUS)
NEW=$(get AWSCURRENT)
curl -sf -u "elastic:$OLD" -X POST "http://$PRIVATE_IP:9200/_security/user/elastic/_password" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"password\":\"$NEW\"}" >/dev/null
echo "elastic password now matches the current secret; restart the temporal-* services"
SCRIPT
